case.title: The tingling the note explained away — symptomatic hypocalcemia after the operation that computed it
case.synthetic_note: SYNTHETIC CASE. The patient is an authored fiction built for teaching; no real patient data exists in this module (design/07, master plan section 8 rule 9: education-only scope). The clinical facts the case uses -- the ATA statement's postoperative-hypoparathyroidism definition, supplementation thresholds and calcitriol criterion (C52), the acute-management criteria and the intravenous calcium gluconate regimen (C53), the albumin-correction formula and the urgency threshold (C54), the bedside signs' appraised performance (C53, C55), the hyperventilation mimic's physiology (C61), the ECG consequences (C59, C60), every reference range (C54, C56-C58) -- trace to the sources registered in cases/parameters.json (C52-C62, consulted in-session at Milestone 57), and the patient's particulars are case data, labelled as such wherever they appear. The operative history is not fiction of the same kind: it is the Theatre module's shipped trace-30 debrief, linked by SHA-256 and matched field-by-field (see theatre_link); the case's calcium course is authored data, not engine output -- the physiology engine's calcium axis (Milestone 58) postdates the operation's own record, and the case cross-checks its authored course against that axis in its physiology_link (Milestone 60) rather than presenting the course as simulated.

history: Total thyroidectomy on postoperative day 0 -- the operation the Theatre module records as trace 30 (see theatre_link and f.thyroidectomy-history); the debrief records the indication as reviewed at the operation against the preoperative diagnosis, imaging and cytology.
Perioral numbness and fingertip tingling since the evening of postoperative day 1, progressing; intermittent cramping of both hands overnight (case data).
A corrected calcium of 7.8 mg/dL measured on postoperative day 1, when the tingling began, and filed without action (case data -- see f.pod1-calcium-filed).
No previous neck surgery or irradiation, no known parathyroid or autoimmune disease, no malabsorptive condition (case data).
No regular medication before admission; no calcium or vitamin D supplementation was started after the operation (case data).

presentation_stages.title: Postoperative day 2: the tingling, and the explanation already attached to it
presentation_stages.narrative: A 57-year-old woman is reviewed on the ward on the morning of postoperative day 2 after a total thyroidectomy -- the operation the Theatre module records as trace 30, whose shipped debrief is this case's operative-history evidence (f.thyroidectomy-history). Since the previous evening she has had numbness and tingling around the mouth and in the fingertips of both hands, worse overnight, with intermittent cramping of the hands. She is frightened by the sensations and breathes fast when they peak. The ward note attributes the symptoms to anxiety with hyperventilation (f.anxiety-attribution). One calcium was measured when the tingling began, on postoperative day 1: corrected 7.8 mg/dL -- below the reference range -- filed without action under the same attribution (f.pod1-calcium-filed). Vitals (case data): temperature 36.9 C, heart rate 96/min, blood pressure 132/80 mmHg, respiratory rate 22/min during symptoms, SpO2 99% on room air. Voice normal; the neck wound flat and dry, no swelling, no stridor. The learner must commit a stage-1 board before any new test is ordered.

presentation_stages.title: Bedside signs
presentation_stages.narrative: The bedside examination battery is performed. Inflating a sphygmomanometer cuff above systolic pressure produces carpopedal spasm of the hand during the inflation -- Trousseau's sign present. Tapping over the facial nerve anterior to the ear produces twitching at the corner of the mouth -- Chvostek's sign present. The voice remains normal, the wound flat, the airway quiet. The learner re-ranks -- and orders.

presentation_stages.title: The panel returns
presentation_stages.narrative: The calcium panel and the ECG return together. Total calcium 7.0 mg/dL with albumin 3.6 g/dL -- corrected 7.3 mg/dL (1.83 mmol/L), down from 7.8 on postoperative day 1. Ionized calcium 0.94 mmol/L. Intact PTH 8 pg/mL -- below the reference range, below the ATA statement's usual lower limit of 12 pg/mL, below its 15 pg/mL postoperative risk threshold. Phosphate 4.9 mg/dL -- above range. Magnesium 1.9 mg/dL -- in range. 25-hydroxyvitamin D 34 ng/mL -- replete. Venous pH 7.44 -- no alkalosis. The ECG shows a QTc of 486 ms. The management-tier block classifies the case at this stage. The learner re-ranks.

presentation_stages.title: Treatment and disposition
presentation_stages.narrative: Management is executed from the tier block and the adjudication: intravenous calcium gluconate under cardiac monitoring, oral calcium and calcitriol alongside, serial calciums until stability -- the calcium-replacement protocol the operation's own dp6 decision had already chosen at t=2760 s (trace 30). The disposition, the follow-up obligations, and the transient-versus-permanent question the case cannot yet answer are written in the management block. The debrief (generated by tools/case_run.py, independently recomputed by tools/case_check.py) scores the attempt's boards against this adjudication.

hypotheses.label: Postoperative hypoparathyroidism -- parathyroid failure after total thyroidectomy

prior.note: VERIFY-FLAGGED PLACEHOLDER, not a measurement: no consulted source gives base rates for this staged presentation in a defined population, so the split is an authoring choice for the exercise, flagged as such wherever it appears. Priced first, and higher than this module's truths usually sit, for a stated reason that is evidence rather than base rate: the linked operation's debrief (trace 30, C62) COMPUTED this outcome at scoring -- the right parathyroid account went unmet (microstep m3.2) and hypocalcemia was declared as its structural consequence -- and the presentation window is the consulted one (C52: hypoPT is the most common complication of bilateral thyroid operations; C53: hypoparathyroidism is most commonly seen after total thyroidectomy, with permanent hypoparathyroidism in 0.5-6% of cases there; the statement's incidence figures for transient disease are far higher). The prior leans on the loop, and says so.

criteria_block.system: ATA statement on postoperative hypoparathyroidism (Orloff 2018): the definition -- a low intact PTH accompanied by hypocalcemia -- evaluated on the case's own atoms, plus the management-tier classification block declared in this case
criteria_block.combination: No score is declared. The diagnosis is the ATA conjunction (corrected calcium below the statement's 8.5 mg/dL line with an intact PTH below its thresholds) and the management consequence is computed by the declared classification block hypocalcemia_management_tier at every stage; neither is asserted by hand.

hypotheses.label: Anxiety with hyperventilation -- the attribution already in the ward note

prior.note: VERIFY-FLAGGED PLACEHOLDER, not a measurement: no consulted source gives base rates for this staged presentation in a defined population, so the split is an authoring choice for the exercise, flagged as such wherever it appears. Priced second because the overlap is genuine and consulted, not caricatured: hyperventilation syndrome's mild-to-moderate picture IS perioral numbness, distal tingling and tetany (C61), produced by a real mechanism this patient is visibly performing (she breathes fast when the symptoms peak). It is also the frame the record already carries (f.anxiety-attribution). The case exists to test whether the learner examines the frame or inherits it -- the prior prices the frame's plausibility, not its truth.

hypotheses.mondo_note: No Mondo class is asserted: the hypothesis names a physiological mimic, not a disease entity; the Milestone 57 OLS pass verified no class for it and none is invented. Its physiology is sourced (C61) and its discriminators are stated findings, not a code.

criteria_block.system: Hyperventilation-syndrome physiology (the Cureus 2023 emergency-department case report, C61)
criteria_block.combination: No score block is declared for the mimic: no consulted source publishes one. Its mechanism is precise, which is what makes it testable -- respiratory alkalosis increases calcium binding to albumin and lowers the IONIZED fraction while the TOTAL calcium does not fall (C61). A low corrected total calcium and a low PTH are therefore findings this hypothesis cannot produce, and a normal venous pH removes its alkalosis; the adjudication weighs the conjunction, and no likelihood ratio is invented for any leg of it.

hypotheses.label: Hypomagnesemia -- functional suppression of PTH secretion

prior.note: VERIFY-FLAGGED PLACEHOLDER, not a measurement: no consulted source gives base rates for this staged presentation in a defined population, so the split is an authoring choice for the exercise, flagged as such wherever it appears. Priced at 0.10: magnesium deficiency is a consulted cause of exactly this physiology (C53 Box 1 lists hypomagnesemia among the causes of hypocalcemia; C54 gives it its mechanism -- magnesium deficiency impairs PTH secretion), it is common after major surgery, and it is the one rival whose treatment differs (repletion before calcium can correct, C54). It is measured in the panel precisely so it can be retired by a number.

hypotheses.mondo_note: No Mondo class is asserted: no hypomagnesemia class was verified in the Milestone 57 OLS pass and none is invented; the hypothesis is carried biochemically -- a magnesium inside its reference range retires it -- rather than ontologically.

criteria_block.system: Cooper & Gittoes 2008 (C54): magnesium deficiency impairs PTH secretion, and hypocalcemia is unlikely to correct without first correcting a low magnesium
criteria_block.combination: No block is declared: the hypothesis lives or dies on one measured value against its MedlinePlus range (C57), which the adjudication reads directly.

hypotheses.label: Postoperative neck hematoma

prior.note: VERIFY-FLAGGED PLACEHOLDER, not a measurement: no consulted source gives base rates for this staged presentation in a defined population, so the split is an authoring choice for the exercise, flagged as such wherever it appears. Priced as the must-not-miss of the fresh neck wound: uncommon, but the one rival that kills by compression, and the operation's own consent record names it (neck hematoma with possible return to theatre, in the linked debrief's m0.2 -- C62). Its examination was complete at stage 1 (flat dry wound, no stridor, normal voice), which is why it sits below the frame on the board; it is carried because a case that omits the airway question on postoperative day 2 after thyroidectomy has failed before it starts.

hypotheses.mondo_note: No Mondo class is asserted: a postoperative hematoma is an event, not a disease class; none was verified for it in the Milestone 57 OLS pass and none is invented.

criteria_block.system: Examination exclusion; the operation's consent record (trace 30, m0.2, via C62) names neck hematoma with possible return to theatre as this operation's priced risk
criteria_block.combination: No block is declared: the hypothesis is excluded by examination -- a flat, dry wound, no stridor, a normal voice (all stage-1 examined facts) -- and no consulted source quantifies it further.

hypotheses.label: Vitamin D inadequacy

prior.note: VERIFY-FLAGGED PLACEHOLDER, not a measurement: no consulted source gives base rates for this staged presentation in a defined population, so the split is an authoring choice for the exercise, flagged as such wherever it appears. Priced lowest of the named rivals: a consulted cause of hypocalcemia (C53 Box 1) and a variable the ATA statement wants assessed around thyroidectomy (C52), but with no mechanism for an onset timed to the operation's second day -- it would have to have been silently present while the glands worked. Carried because the panel measures it and the statement asks after it, not because the timing argues for it.

hypotheses.mondo_note: No Mondo class is asserted: no vitamin-D-inadequacy class was verified in the Milestone 57 OLS pass and none is invented; the hypothesis is carried on its measured value against the consulted inadequacy line (C53).

criteria_block.system: Fong & Khan 2012 (C53): vitamin D inadequacy (25(OH)D < 75 nmol/L) as a cause of hypocalcemia, read against the same review's hypoparathyroid profile (hyperphosphatemia)
criteria_block.combination: No block is declared: the hypothesis is weighed on two measured legs -- a 25(OH)D above the consulted inadequacy line, and a phosphate ABOVE range, where a vitamin-D-driven hypocalcemia pulls phosphate down with failed absorption, not up; the hypoparathyroid profile names hyperphosphatemia as the opposite pattern (C53).

hypotheses.label: Other / unspecified cause

prior.note: VERIFY-FLAGGED PLACEHOLDER, not a measurement: no consulted source gives base rates for this staged presentation in a defined population, so the split is an authoring choice for the exercise, flagged as such wherever it appears. The residual bucket, deliberately the second-largest mass on the board: the honest remainder for causes the consulted sources name but this case does not stage (C53 Box 1 also lists chronic kidney disease, pancreatitis, citrate and phosphate loads, and drug causes -- none of which this patient's record supports) and for the causes nobody has named. hypotheses.mondo_note: Residual hypothesis: by construction it names no single condition, so no Mondo class is asserted for it. It exists so the board's mass is honest -- the named five are not the world -- and it retires arithmetically as the sourced evidence lands on the truth.

findings.text: The patient is 57 years old (case data). Priced in the differential only as a post-surgical adult; no consulted source quantifies age's effect on this differential and none is invented.

OPERATIVE HISTORY (the loop evidence item -- read from theatre/debriefs/trace-30-thyroid-parathyroid-unaccounted.debrief.json, not retyped from memory; the checker re-reads that file and matches every fact stated here). The total thyroidectomy of postoperative day 0 is the Theatre's shipped trace-30 attempt on proc.thyroidectomy.total. The attempt's verdict was PASS: checklist 42 of 43 microsteps -- the one unperformed microstep is m3.2, the right parathyroid account; safety gate 3 of 4; management 5 of 5. The debrief records the error err.parathyroid-unaccounted at t=2880 s and computes the complication this case now presents: kind hypocalcemia, resolved structure gland.parathyroid-glands, recognised: false in the operation's own record -- with the management the operation's decision dp6 had already chosen at t=2760 s: calcium-replacement-protocol. File SHA-256 a389d3810b5b1c18a37743d40b10c71f1ababf4e601103e5f6e105b8b1e8c120 (recorded in theatre_link; the checker recomputes it).

Perioral numbness and tingling with tingling in the fingertips of both hands, present since the evening of postoperative day 1 and progressing, with intermittent cramping of both hands overnight (case data). The consulted sources name this exact picture as hypocalcemia's common presentation -- paresthesia, circumoral numbness, muscle cramps and tetany (C53) -- and as the presenting symptoms of postoperative hypoparathyroidism (C52). It is also, verbatim, the mild-to-moderate picture of hyperventilation syndrome (C61). The overlap is the case.

The ward note from postoperative day 1 attributes the tingling to anxiety with hyperventilation: the patient is visibly frightened by the sensations and breathes fast when they peak (case data). The attribution is recorded here as a finding because it is evidence -- of the frame, not of the physiology. Nothing in the note records a calcium being acted on, a bedside sign being elicited, or the operation's computed outcome being read.

Postoperative day 1, when the tingling began: total calcium 7.7 mg/dL, albumin 3.9 g/dL -- corrected 7.8 mg/dL (7.7 + 0.8 x (4.0 - 3.9) = 7.78, rounded; the albumin correction of C54), BELOW the reference range and below the ATA statement's 8.5 mg/dL hypocalcemia line (C52). It was filed without action under the anxiety attribution (f.anxiety-attribution). The case's quietest fact and its most expensive one: the discriminating evidence existed a full day before the case opens, and the frame absorbed it. The stage-3 panel's 7.3 mg/dL is therefore a DECLINE on sequential measurements -- the exact condition the ATA calcitriol criterion (C52) turns on.

Voice normal, no hoarseness (case data). Read two ways: the operation's recurrent-laryngeal-nerve criteria were met on both sides in the linked debrief (trace 30), and a normal voice on day 2 is consistent with that record; and against the hematoma hypothesis, whose airway compression would not leave the voice untouched.

Neck swelling ABSENT: the wound is flat and dry, no expanding mass, no ecchymosis (case data). The hematoma hypothesis's central examined fact, assessed zero at stage 1 -- with f.stridor and f.voice-normal it retires the airway question on examination, which is how the case can afford to spend its stages on the calcium.

Stridor ABSENT: the airway is quiet at rest and on exertion in the bed (case data). With the flat wound, the finding that lets the team treat this as a metabolic problem rather than a surgical emergency -- stated explicitly because on postoperative day 2 after thyroidectomy the distinction is the first decision, not a detail.
Heart rate 96/min, regular (case data). Consistent with a frightened, symptomatic patient; no consulted source makes it discriminate this differential and it moves no board.

Respiratory rate 22/min during symptom peaks (case data). The frame's best evidence: she does breathe fast when the tingling peaks. What it cannot show is causation -- the tingling frightens her, and either direction produces a rate of 22. The discriminator is chemical, not observational (f.no-alkalosis, f.hypocalcemia-confirmed).
Blood pressure 132/80 mmHg (case data). No hypotension; nothing in the consulted sources makes this discriminate.
Oxygen saturation 99% on room air (case data). Normoxia: whatever is producing the tingling is not hypoxemia.
Temperature 36.9 C -- afebrile (case data). No febrile or septic process is staged; the finding is recorded so the absence is an assessed zero, not an omission.

Trousseau's sign present: carpopedal spasm of the hand appearing during a 3-minute sphygmomanometer cuff inflation above systolic pressure, at about two minutes (case data; the manoeuvre as described in C53 and shown in C55). The case's only likelihood-ratio finding. C53 calls it the more reliable of the two bedside signs; the classic figures (C55) put it in 94% of hypocalcemic patients and 1% of people with normal calcium. The LR is computed at the conservative end of the consulted pair (derivation in cases/parameters.json), and the counterweight travels with it in the lr note: in the population this patient actually belongs to -- post-thyroidectomy -- a 2016 cohort found the sign in only 23.5% of hypocalcemic patients, so the board's stage-2 confidence outruns what the sign alone earns, and the adjudication rests on the biochemistry and the tier block, not on this number.

lr.note: LR+ 23.5, computed at the conservative end of the consulted pair: sensitivity 0.94 (stated by both C53 and C55), false-positive rate taken as 0.04 -- the least favourable end of C53's stated 1% to 4% in healthy people (C55 states 1%, which would give 94.0). Derivation in cases/parameters.json. The appraisal travels with the number: a 2016 post-thyroidectomy cohort found Trousseau's sign in only 23.5% of hypocalcemic patients -- in-context sensitivity far below the classic figure -- so this LR is the board's arithmetic from the consulted classic pair, disclosed as such, and the adjudication deliberately rests on the biochemistry (f.hypocalcemia-confirmed, f.pth-low) and the tier block.

findings.text: Chvostek's sign present: twitching at the corner of the mouth on tapping over the facial nerve anterior to the ear (case data; elicitation as C53 describes). Carried WITHOUT a likelihood ratio, deliberately: the consulted appraisal is divided -- C55 records the sign absent in about a third of patients with hypocalcemia and present in about 10% of people with normal calcium -- and the post-thyroidectomy cohort found it in fewer still (11.8%). It corroborates the Trousseau finding at the bedside; it moves no board. The tier block reads it only as one atom of the symptomatic input, where its presence is not load-bearing (the paresthesias and the Trousseau sign satisfy that input without it).

Hypocalcemia CONFIRMED on the corrected value: total calcium 7.0 mg/dL with albumin 3.6 g/dL corrects to 7.3 mg/dL (7.0 + 0.8 x (4.0 - 3.6) = 7.32, rounded; in SI: 1.75 + 0.02 x (40 - 36) = 1.83 mmol/L -- the C54 correction to a reference albumin of 40 g/L). Below the reference range (C54: 2.10-2.60 mmol/L, rendered 8.4-10.4 mg/dL), below the ATA statement's 8.5 mg/dL hypocalcemia line (C52), and below the 1.9 mmol/L urgency threshold both acute sources state (C53, C54; rendered 7.6 mg/dL). The ionized fraction agrees independently: 0.94 mmol/L (lab.ionized-calcium) -- the pair of numbers the anxiety hypothesis cannot produce, because hyperventilation lowers the ionized fraction while the TOTAL does not fall (C61), and here both have fallen.

Intact PTH 8 pg/mL: below the MedlinePlus reference range (10-65 pg/mL, C56), below the ATA statement's usual lower limit of the laboratory standard (12 pg/mL), and below its postoperative risk threshold (15 pg/mL) (C52). With the corrected calcium it completes the ATA definition of postoperative hypoparathyroidism -- a low intact PTH accompanied by hypocalcemia -- on the case's own atoms. The second fact the mimic cannot produce: intact glands answer a true ionized fall by raising PTH; these glands cannot answer at all.

Phosphate 4.9 mg/dL -- above the MedlinePlus adult range (2.8-4.5 mg/dL, C58). The hypoparathyroid profile's third limb: C53 states that hypoparathyroidism shows hypocalcemia with a low or inappropriately normal PTH and HYPERPHOSPHATEMIA -- PTH is phosphaturic, and without it phosphate accumulates. The same value argues against the vitamin-D rival, whose mechanism (failed intestinal absorption) pulls phosphate down, not up.

Magnesium 1.9 mg/dL -- inside the MedlinePlus range (1.7-2.2 mg/dL, C57). One measured value retires two things: the hypomagnesemia hypothesis (no deficiency exists to suppress PTH secretion, C54) and the management caveat C54 attaches to it -- hypocalcemia unlikely to correct without first correcting a low magnesium. No correction is needed, so calcium replacement proceeds on the tier block's terms.
25-hydroxyvitamin D 34 ng/mL (about 85 nmol/L) -- above the inadequacy line the consulted review states (25(OH)D < 75 nmol/L, C53). The nutritional rival is retired by its own consulted threshold.

Venous pH 7.44 on the panel draw (meas.venous-ph) -- no alkalosis. The mimic's mechanism REQUIRES an alkalosis: hyperventilation raises pH, the raised pH increases calcium binding to albumin, and the ionized fraction falls with the total unchanged (C61). A normal pH beside a low total calcium and a low PTH is a pattern the anxiety hypothesis has no mechanism to produce. The finding is recorded so the exclusion is a measurement, not a preference.

ECG: QTc 486 ms -- prolonged for a woman (the consulted ECG review's threshold: > 450 ms in women, C60), by prolongation of the ST segment, the hypocalcemia pattern (C59: low ionized calcium prolongs the ST segment and the QT with it; its worked case shows a QTc of 533 ms at a total calcium of 5.0 mg/dL). Below the 500 ms band C59 associates with increased arrhythmia risk. The finding carries no likelihood ratio and settles no tier input; its role is management safety -- cardiac monitoring during intravenous calcium is necessary (C53), and this tracing is why. The machinery will classify the ECG order non-contributory; the case records that verdict as a limit of the classification, not of the order.

labs.interpretation: The raw total that corrects to 7.8 mg/dL at the day's albumin of 3.9 g/dL (lab.corrected-calcium-pod1). Measured when the tingling began and filed without action (f.pod1-calcium-filed). Corrected for albumin by C54's formula (adjust to a reference albumin of 40 g/L); range is C54's normal serum calcium 2.10-2.60 mmol/L rendered in mg/dL.

7.7 + 0.8 x (4.0 - 3.9) = 7.78, rounded to 7.8 (C54's correction). Below the reference range and below the ATA statement's 8.5 mg/dL hypocalcemia line (C52) on the day the symptoms started. This is the value the stage-3 panel declines FROM -- 'declining on sequential measurements' in the ATA calcitriol criterion (C52) is a comparison, and this is its first term.

The raw total that corrects to 7.3 mg/dL at albumin 3.6 g/dL (lab.corrected-calcium). Corrected for albumin by C54's formula (adjust to a reference albumin of 40 g/L); range is C54's normal serum calcium 2.10-2.60 mmol/L rendered in mg/dL.

7.0 + 0.8 x (4.0 - 3.6) = 7.32, rounded to 7.3 mg/dL; SI: 1.75 + 0.02 x (40 - 36) = 1.83 mmol/L (C54). Below the ATA hypocalcemia line (8.5 mg/dL, C52) and below the 1.9 mmol/L urgency threshold C53 and C54 both state (rendered 7.6 mg/dL) -- one of the three independent intravenous-tier limbs. Declined from 7.8 mg/dL on postoperative day 1: the sequential decline the ATA calcitriol criterion (C52) turns on.

Below the reference range printed in the consulted hyperventilation case report's own laboratory table (1.15-1.33 mmol/L, C61), below the ATA supplementation threshold (1.1 mmol/L, C52) and below the intravenous criterion (< 1.0 mmol/L, C53) -- the second independent intravenous limb. The physiologically active fraction: the number that explains the symptoms, and the number hyperventilation can lower only by leaving the total unchanged (C61) -- which the total refutes.

Below the MedlinePlus range (10-65 pg/mL, C56), below the ATA statement's usual lower limit of the laboratory standard (12 pg/mL) and below its postoperative risk threshold (15 pg/mL, C52) -- the tier block's PTH input. With the corrected calcium, the ATA definition of postoperative hypoparathyroidism is met on the case's own atoms (C52).
Inside the MedlinePlus range (1.7-2.2 mg/dL, C57): the hypomagnesemia hypothesis is retired and the C54 caveat (correct magnesium first) is discharged by measurement.
Above the MedlinePlus adult range (2.8-4.5 mg/dL, C58): the hypoparathyroid profile's hyperphosphatemia limb (C53) and the argument against the vitamin-D rival, whose mechanism pulls phosphate down.

34 ng/mL (about 85 nmol/L). The reference_range records only a lower bound, deliberately: the consulted review states an inadequacy line (25(OH)D < 75 nmol/L, C53), rendered here as its equivalent 30 ng/mL, and no consulted source states an upper bound -- so none is printed. The value sits above the inadequacy line: replete; the nutritional rival is retired by its own consulted threshold.

measurements.name: Albumin, postoperative day 1
measurements.interpretation: The albumin the day-1 correction turns on: 7.7 + 0.8 x (4.0 - 3.9) = 7.78 (C54). Recorded as a measurement, not a lab, because no consulted source states an albumin reference range and none is printed.

measurements.name: Albumin
measurements.interpretation: The albumin the stage-3 correction turns on: 7.0 + 0.8 x (4.0 - 3.6) = 7.32 mg/dL (SI: 1.75 + 0.02 x (40 - 36) = 1.83 mmol/L; C54). Recorded as a measurement for the same reason as meas.albumin-pod1.

measurements.name: Venous pH
measurements.interpretation: No alkalosis: the mimic's required mechanism is absent (f.no-alkalosis, C61). Carried as a measurement; no reference range is claimed for it from any consulted source -- C53 lists pH among the basic investigations for hypocalcemia, and the case reads the value for the single question it answers.

measurements.name: QTc interval
measurements.interpretation: Prolonged for a woman (> 450 ms, C60), by ST-segment prolongation (C59); below the 500 ms arrhythmia-risk band (C59). See f.qt-prolonged.

available_tests.name: Bedside tetany-sign examination
available_tests.note: The bedside battery: Trousseau's and Chvostek's manoeuvres, with re-examination of voice, wound and airway. The machinery classifies it discriminating -- its Trousseau yield carries the case's only likelihood ratio and retires every rival across the rule-out line at stage 2. The note the case insists travel with that verdict: the classification is the board's arithmetic from the consulted classic pair, and the board's stage-2 confidence outruns the sign's in-context performance (see f.trousseau-sign); the adjudication does not rest on it.

available_tests.name: Calcium panel (corrected/ionized calcium, PTH, magnesium, phosphate, vitamin D, albumin, venous pH)
available_tests.note: The Fong & Khan Box 2 panel (C53): corrected calcium, phosphate, magnesium, PTH, 25-hydroxyvitamin D and pH as basic investigations, ionized calcium from its further-investigations list, albumin for the C54 correction. The machinery classifies it criteria-completing: it settles the management tier's inputs (the tier classifies at stage 3 on its return) and moves no board, because no consulted source quantifies a likelihood ratio for a calcium value and none is invented. It is also, in the adjudication's reading, the case's decisive order -- the one whose postoperative-day-1 forerunner was drawn and filed unactioned.

available_tests.name: 12-lead ECG
available_tests.note: Ordered for the QT. The machinery classifies it non-contributory -- no likelihood ratio, no tier input -- and the case keeps the order and the verdict side by side: prolonged QT is a consulted presentation of hypocalcemia (C53 lists it; C59 gives the mechanism), the QTc prices the arrhythmia risk the intravenous infusion must be monitored against (C59's 500 ms band; C53's cardiac-monitoring requirement), and a classification system that counts only diagnostic motion will call a safety measurement non-contributory. Recorded as a limit of the instrument, in the instrument's own output.

criteria_blocks.label: Hypocalcemia management tier (post-thyroidectomy)
criteria_blocks.system: Management tiers for post-thyroidectomy hypocalcemia, ASSEMBLED at Milestone 57 from three consulted sources: the ATA statement's supplementation thresholds and calcitriol criterion (C52), the Fong & Khan acute-management criteria for intravenous calcium (C53), and the Cooper & Gittoes urgency threshold (C54). No consulted source publishes this exact three-tier block; every threshold inside it is one a consulted source states, and the assembly is disclosed rather than dressed as a quotation.

result.label: Intravenous calcium indicated -- symptomatic hypocalcemia with corrected calcium below 1.9 mmol/L: IV calcium gluconate under cardiac monitoring, oral calcium and calcitriol alongside (C53 criteria; the C52 calcitriol criterion -- symptomatic with calcium declining on sequential measurements -- is also met)
Intravenous calcium indicated -- symptomatic hypocalcemia with ionized calcium below 1.0 mmol/L (C53)
Intravenous calcium indicated -- corrected calcium below 1.9 mmol/L: urgent assessment and treatment (C53, C54)
Intravenous calcium indicated -- ionized calcium below 1.0 mmol/L (C53)

ground_truth.diagnosis: Postoperative hypoparathyroidism after total thyroidectomy. The operation's per-side parathyroid gate priced exactly this: the right parathyroid account (microstep m3.2) went unmet in trace 30, and hypocalcemia was computed at scoring as the structural outcome on gland.parathyroid-glands. It declares clinically on postoperative days 1-2 as symptomatic hypocalcemia: perioral and digital paresthesias progressing to cramps (POD1 evening onward), Trousseau's and Chvostek's signs present, corrected calcium 7.3 mg/dL (1.83 mmol/L) fallen from 7.8, ionized calcium 0.94 mmol/L, intact PTH 8 pg/mL, phosphate 4.9 mg/dL, magnesium normal, vitamin D replete, venous pH normal, QTc 486 ms. Managed on the intravenous tier: IV calcium gluconate under cardiac monitoring with oral calcium and calcitriol alongside -- the calcium-replacement protocol the operation's dp6 decision had already chosen. Whether the failure is transient or permanent is not knowable at postoperative day 2: the ATA statement's line is 6 months (C52), and the case records the diagnosis at the time it is made, not the prognosis nobody can yet give.

The calcium course in this case remains authored data, every value checked against the consulted sources (C52-C54) and the albumin-correction arithmetic re-derived by the checker; it is not simulation output and is never presented as such. See physiology_link.

management.disposition: Intravenous calcium gluconate 10 percent, two 10 mL ampoules (2 g salt) diluted in 100 mL of 5 percent dextrose, infused over 10 minutes under CARDIAC MONITORING -- the regimen both acute sources state (C53: 10-20 mL of 10% calcium gluconate in 50-100 mL D5W over 5-10 minutes, cardiac monitoring during IV calcium necessary; C54 concurs: 10 mL of 10% calcium gluconate in 50-100 mL of 5% dextrose over 10 minutes, gluconate preferred over chloride). All three of C53's intravenous limbs are met independently -- symptomatic, corrected calcium below 1.9 mmol/L, ionized below 1.0 mmol/L -- and the tier block's first rule fires on the conjunction. Alongside: oral calcium to the ATA postoperative regimen, 400-1200 mg of elemental calcium per day (1-3 g calcium carbonate) in divided doses (C52), and calcitriol 0.25-0.5 micrograms twice daily -- started on the statement's exact criterion (symptomatic hypocalcemia with calcium declining on sequential measurements, 7.8 -> 7.3 mg/dL, C52), in the agent both reviews require for PTH deficiency (C53: oral calcium supplements and calcitriol; C54: calcitriol or alfacalcidol rather than conventional vitamin D doses). Serial serum calcium levels until stable, with monitoring for REBOUND hypercalcemia as the surviving glands recover (C52). Magnesium is normal, so no repletion precedes the calcium (C54's caveat discharged by measurement). Endocrine and operating-surgeon follow-up; discharge when symptoms have resolved and calcium is stable or rising on the oral regimen, with written safety-netting on the symptoms of recurrence. The transient-versus-permanent question is carried openly: it cannot be answered before the ATA statement's 6-month line (C52), and the follow-up, not this encounter, answers it. This disposition EXECUTES the calcium-replacement protocol the operation's own dp6 decision chose at t=2760 s (trace 30, C62) -- the loop the theatre_link records is closed by management, not just by history.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Oral supplementation alone (the ATA mild-to-moderate route, C52)
alternatives_considered.reason_refused: The intravenous tier is met three independent ways (C53): she is symptomatic, her corrected calcium is below 1.9 mmol/L, and her ionized calcium is below 1.0 mmol/L. The oral route is the right answer to a milder case; this is not it, and the tier block -- not preference -- says so.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Reassurance and anxiolysis for hyperventilation (the stage-1 frame)
alternatives_considered.reason_refused: The frame's physiology cannot produce the findings: a low TOTAL calcium (C61), a low PTH, and a normal venous pH. Treating the frame would repeat the day-1 error with the panel on the chart.
Both acute sources prefer gluconate (C53, C54); chloride is the more potent and more irritant salt and nothing in this presentation prices that trade in its favour.
